command: git ls-files mbt, then count the .mbt files and package directories

definitions.library_source_files: tracked *.mbt under mbt/, excluding mbt/tests/ and mbt/examples/
definitions.packages: directories directly under mbt/ that carry a moon.pkg
definitions.root_imports: distinct riantr/snn_mbt/* entries imported by mbt/moon.pkg
definitions.example_packages: directories under mbt/examples/ that carry a moon.pkg
definitions.library_lines: newline count of every tracked library *.mbt under mbt/ (rounded_facts, not facts)
definitions.rl_lines: newline count of the tracked *.mbt under mbt/rl/ (rounded_facts, not facts)
definitions.synapse_lines: newline count of the tracked *.mbt under mbt/synapse/ (rounded_facts, not facts)
definitions.ported_files: library files that name one of the upstream Julia packages and are not in a harness package

provenance.note: How a file is counted as PORTED, which is the one thing the documentation's '74 of the 301' depends on. A file counts as ported when its text names one of the upstream_packages -- the three Julia packages this port is translated from -- and it is not in one of the harness_packages. Naming an upstream is the marker of a translation: it is how a translated file says which upstream file it came from, whether it names the file itself (`SNNModels.jl/src/utils/structs.jl`) or the symbol (`compose(; kwargs...)`). The harness packages are excluded because they are QA scaffolding rather than ported code, and because mbt/fuzz_props/main.mbt names SpikingNeuralNetworks.jl in prose -- it says the project IS a port of it -- without being a translation of anything. That exclusion is what makes the aggregate agree with the package table, which lists the harness packages as 'original'. The rule lives here, next to the numbers it defines, so that changing what 'ported' means is a reviewable edit to a data file rather than an edit to the harness.

claims.pattern: the full table — {ported_files} of the {library_source_files}\s+library files are translations
the widest fan-out is `infra` at {widest_fan_out} packages
That is {ported_files} of the {library_source_files} library source files

note: The shape of the tree, and the counts the documentation quotes from it. These are pinned because every one of them had already drifted, and the reason they drifted is worth recording: the documentation said 732 source files because the count came from a directory walk, and a walk sees the 400 vendored .mbt files that `moon update` leaves in mbt/.mooncakes/ and the four scratch files under the gitignored mbt/_disabled/ and mbt/_new_lstm/ directories. That is the dependency cache, not this package's source. The counts here come from `git ls-files`, which sees what the repository actually tracks, so the vendored cache cannot inflate them again. The numbers also drifted apart from each other -- the root README said 681 source files and 23 packages while the package README said 732 and 299 -- because two documents each carried its own count. Pinning them here means there is one number and one place to update it. The `docs` gate measures the tree, compares it with this file, and then checks that both READMEs still quote it: tree -> baseline -> documentation cannot come apart. Two of the numbers are BORROWED from the gate that owns them -- the formatter's distance from canonical form from verify/fmt_baseline.json, and the dependency depth and the widest fan-out from verify/deps_baseline.json -- so the documentation is checked against the measurement the owning gate actually makes, rather than against a second copy of it. Every sentence of a claim's shape must carry the pinned number, not merely one of them, because a wrong count that happens to sit beside a right one is still wrong. The counts that the documentation quotes ON PURPOSE as approximations -- 'about 65,300 lines' -- are listed under rounded_claims and checked by rounding the measurement the same way, so the rounding is a rule rather than a tolerance fitted to whatever the prose happened to say. Any change to these counts must update this file and the quoted counts in the same commit.
